Advanced ATC

Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity

A communications system using 5G cellular technology in the C-band spectrum for high-speed, low-latency data transfer to and from aircraft (ICAO GANP, SESAR).

Quick answer: A communications system using 5G cellular technology in the C-band spectrum for high-speed, low-latency data transfer to and from aircraft (ICAO GANP, SESAR).

Quick answer

Why it matters

Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity matters because it supports clear communication in Advanced ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Questions and answers

What is Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity?

In this glossary, Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity refers to: A communications system using 5G cellular technology in the C-band spectrum for high-speed, low-latency data transfer to and from aircraft (ICAO GANP, SESAR).

How is Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity provided uninterrupted inflight streaming and rapid ground communications."

Why does Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity matter in aviation?

Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity matters because it supports clear communication in Advanced ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity?

Fifth-Generation C-Band Connectivity is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.
